extracted.intended_audience: Reuters reporters, desk editors and newsroom newsroom staff
extracted.subtask_description: Operational style and editing guidelines for Reuters newsroom staff covering when to correct, refile or repeat stories; how to code stories and handle RICs; and standards for presentation (headlines, datelines, bylines, bullets, links, service messages, schedules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections: RIC errors
rubrics_metrics.description: When the RIC used is not that of the company in the news. A wrong RIC is an error of fact in a story and must be corrected, just like any other substantive error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a RIC belongs to no other company and links to a blank data page, the story should be refiled to remove the dead RIC and replace it with an active RIC. Deskers must check RICs as they would any other checkable fact in the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections: Numerical data (DATA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nearly every error that involves a number requires a correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include any numeric mistakes (amounts, percentages, figures) as corrections rather than updates or refiles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections: Million vs billion (scale words)
rubrics_metrics.description: Corrections are necessary when the words 'million' or 'billion' are wrong or have been dropped.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fix immediately — these errors materially change meaning and can mislead readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections: Dates and time periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Wrong dates, months or years in the text should be corrected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This excludes datelines and days of the week in the first paragraph which often can be addressed with a refile unless the meaning changes (e.g., wrong century). Advisory lines should indicate what was corrected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections: Quotes that change meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: Any error in a quote that changes the meaning of the sentence requires a correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is unacceptable to drop the quote in an update instead of issuing a correction. Minor extra or missing words without meaning change can be refiles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections: Prices and directions of price moves
rubrics_metrics.description: It is unacceptable to issue an update rather than a correction when the wrong price for a stock, bond or other asset is published, or when the story reports the wrong direction of a price change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: if the price changed incrementally while the story was being filed. Always correct substantive price errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections: Background information
rubrics_metrics.description: Background information that is wrong should be corrected even if it is not primary to the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wrong background can harm credibility; include an advisory line explaining the correction (example given in handbook).

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections: Proper names with confusing misspellings
rubrics_metrics.description: Names of people, places, companies and organisations should be corrected when a misspelling creates confusion or when an erroneous name has been substituted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a refile to correct obvious typos in proper names (e.g., President Georeg Bush). If an erroneous name substitutes a different person (e.g., Jeb vs George W.), issue a correction and explain in advisory/trashline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections: General content errors (analyses/descriptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptions, analyses or explanations that are erroneous should be corrected even if republished from a previous story or not of primary importance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advisory lines should specify the erroneous description (example: wrongly described XYZ Co as the largest widget maker).

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections: Dropped words that change meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: When a missing word changes the meaning of a sentence, a correction is necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'He was found guilty' vs 'He was found not guilty'. If the dropped word does not change meaning, use a refile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections: Time references
rubrics_metrics.description: Corrections of time references should carry advisory lines indicating the corrected time/month/period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example advisory: 'Corrects month measured by housing data to June instead of July.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Alerts: special handling of mistakes
rubrics_metrics.description: Mistakes in Alerts raise the special issue of timings and how to remediate them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Errors that would merit refiles are often better left unaddressed in Alerts; however, any mistake involving a number in Alerts should be corrected. All Alert mistakes should be sent to the appropriate editing desk rather than handled independently by field staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to Refile: RICs (inactive/dead symbols)
rubrics_metrics.description: Refile stories that contain wrong RICs only when the symbol used belongs to no other company and links to a blank data page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trashline example: 'Refiles to correct inactive stock symbol in paragraph 4.' If a RIC belonging to another company is mistakenly used, a correction (not a refile) is required (trashline: 'Corrects stock symbol ... to ABC.N from ABC.O').

rubrics_metrics.name: When to Refile: Dateline errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Use refile for errors in datelines, including location and date, unless either would have an important bearing on the meaning of the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Corrects dateline from FRANKFURT to Brussels' (would be correction if meaningful) vs routine dateline fixes handled as refiles.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to Refile: Day of the week errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Refile when the wrong day of the week appears in the lead unless it distorts the significance of the news or applies to a day in the future.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example advisory: 'Corrects day in first paragraph to Tuesday from Monday.'

rubrics_metrics.name: When to Refile: Time conversions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use refile for simple time conversions when the time being converted is correct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'Corrects time in paragraph 3 to 1350 GMT from 1550 GMT.'

rubrics_metrics.name: When to Refile: Spelling and typographical errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Use refile for typographical errors of common words or most spelling mistakes in proper names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trashline examples: 'Fixes typo in 10th paragraph' or 'Corrects spelling of Greenspan in final paragraph.'

rubrics_metrics.name: When to Refile: Names (minor reference formatting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use refile to correct name references such as 'President Bush' to 'President George W. Bush' or fix first-reference formatting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trashline example: 'Refiles to correct name in paragraph 2 to President George W. Bush.' If a wrong person was named (substituted name), use correction instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to Refile: Ages
rubrics_metrics.description: Use refile to correct the age of an individual unless the mistake distorts the meaning of the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trashline example: 'Refiles to correct age in paragraph 6 to 53 years old.' If distortion occurs, use correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to Refile: Titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Use refile to correct minor mistakes in titles (e.g., senior vice president instead of vice president).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: But use CORRECTED for errors that could have bigger ramifications (e.g., chief financial officer instead of chief executive). Desk head decides in doubtful cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to Refile: Adds or deletes word (minor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use refile to insert dropped words or delete extraneous ones unless the dropped/present word distorts meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example refile: 'Corrects to add dropped word executive in paragraph 10.' Words like 'not', 'million' or 'percent' that alter meaning require corrections, not refiles.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to Repeat: Adding codes and RICs
rubrics_metrics.description: Use repeats to widen distribution when adding codes and RICs to a story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advisory line: 'Repeats to widen distribution.' Remove media codes from the repeat as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to Repeat: Adding bylines or taglines
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeat when adding bylines or taglines to a previously filed story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advisory line: 'Repeats to adds byline.'

rubrics_metrics.name: When to Repeat: Changing slugs or USNs
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeat to change story slug used by some customers or to move to a new story number (USN).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trashline examples: 'Repeats to change story label' or 'Repeats to new story number. Remove media codes from the repeat.' If changing slug for media customers, notify media codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to Repeat: Removing attached story or attaching to alerts
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeat to remove a story attached to the bottom of text or to attach text to news alerts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trashlines: 'Repeats to remove story attached to bottom of text' and 'Repeats to attach text to news alerts. Remove any media codes from the repeat.'

rubrics_metrics.name: When to Repeat: Repeating for timing around data or events
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeat a story ahead of data or events or repeat a story first published on a previous day when appropriate for distribution timing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trashline examples: 'Repeats story published on Monday ahead of data due at (time)' and 'Repeats story first published on Sunday.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Coding guideline: Topic codes usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Topic codes are applied to stories ABOUT a topic, not to stories merely of interest to a particular sector or country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the topic code doesn't explain what the story is about, don't use it (e.g., an economic indicator of forex interest is NOT a forex story and should not take FRX). Use OPEC/IMF/G7/EU codes only for stories ABOUT those organisations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coding guideline: Product codes and topic codes after filing
rubrics_metrics.description: It is possible to add topic codes after the story is filed but NOT product codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can add product codes to a newsbreak covering an alert. To add a topic code post-file, send a 'dummy' page with same USN using at least one product code from the original story and include a full headline and something in the text field (even a period).

rubrics_metrics.name: Coding guideline: Minimum codes reporters should apply
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories landing on desks should at least carry the country topic code, the regional topic code (EMRG if an emerging market) and the main subject code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters, especially specialists, should try to apply topic codes to stories they file to desks to avoid sloppy coding and missed readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: RICs: inclusion and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: RICs must be included in the Lynx Editor header field and in the story itself; company RIC follows the first mention of a company in the body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Economic indicator RICs should be added for the specific story on the latest release but not for every mention of the data. RICs must also be entered into the Lynx Alerting table when injecting live data updates to screens.

rubrics_metrics.name: RICs: format and types (listed, unlisted, ADR/GDR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Traditional company RICs include exchange identifiers (e.g., IBM.N). Unlisted companies use square brackets and a UL identifier (e.g., [TPG.UL]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the mother RIC on first reference. For dual-listed companies, insert ADR/GDR RICs in the copy where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: RICs: lookup and verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the RIC look-up in Lynx Editor to find the correct RIC; do not guess.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methods: compare FULL name in the RIC list, use cemplookup URL, type RIC into 3000 Xtra/Eikon news or QUOTE windows to verify trading and prior stories, ensure RIC matches previous stories. If a RIC search pulls no results, investigate or ask senior reporters.

rubrics_metrics.name: RICs: stripping and bad-impact warning
rubrics_metrics.description: Strip all RICs from copy going to media subscribers and Business News Schedules. A wrong company RIC, especially linked to 'bad news', can have serious impact on the wrongly identified company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dead or wrong RICs reduce visibility for clients and should be cleaned (refiles for dead RICs). Tell your desk head when you find incorrect/problematic RICs.

rubrics_metrics.name: RICs: tips to avoid errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical tips to avoid RIC errors: avoid false RICs of similarly named companies, avoid short name searches, use full company name with correct capitalization, be wary of internal capitals and unusual punctuation, know common acronyms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some major companies have multiple RICs; use mother RIC on first reference. When in doubt, ask senior reporters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service messages: tone, content and format
rubrics_metrics.description: Service messages are in-house editorial messages that should be short, simple, to the point and polite; humour and inappropriate language must be avoided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational news editing done by phone or messaging should be followed up with a service message or email. Do not send full stories in service messages unless asked. Sensitive stories should be sent with **ATTN EDITOR** flag and via regular filing codes; precede with a service message outlining concerns. Message label format: bureau short form + timestamp + one-word subject (sample provided). Service messages are not private and can be mis-coded onto client circuits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory lines (Trash lines / EDS NOTE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Advisory lines at the top of Updates advise clients of additional new details and help decide whether re-editing is needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep to one line (no more than two), enclosed in brackets, indent one space, start with a capital letter. Be specific (e.g., '(Adds prime minister's reaction in paragraph 3, updates death toll in paragraph 4)'). Do not start advisory with 'eds' or 'eds note'; avoid journalese.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bullet points: form and usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Bullet points break complicated information into digestible form and highlight main elements; used in briefs, updates, wrapups, interviews, market reports and factboxes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules: succinct, active voice, present tense; each preceded by an asterisk (*); minimum 2, maximum 5 (BRIEF exception: can exceed 5); cannot exceed one line (~10 words); can be analytical or interpretative; both reporters and desk editors can write them. Special rules for PREVIEW ('* What:' and '* When:' first two bullets) and market reports (avoid bullets with market prices in narrative reports).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bylines: when to byline stories
rubrics_metrics.description: A correspondent's byline indicates ownership and responsibility for substantial reporting. Do not byline routine reporting of press statements, releases, or pickups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any news story with original reporting may carry a byline regardless of length. Double bylines may be used for significant reporting by two individuals but sparingly; more than two requires senior editor approval. Double dateline stories that are bylined should carry bylines from each location.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-heads (sub-heads)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-heads break long copy into digestible morsels; used in stories of 500 or more words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sub-heads should be 2-4 words, in UPPER CASE, simple, informative and unbiased. Insert a blank line before the cross-head. One or two cross-heads for 500-600 words; 3-4 for ~800 words. Avoid breaking flow or splitting quotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Links formatting for desktop and media
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific bracket conventions to link to other Reuters stories, RICs, graphics, video or source documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use [ID:nXXXXXX] for Reuters stories, <XX.X> for RICs, and double round brackets ((http://...)) for URLs. These brackets preserve links for desktop clients but delete them for media clients. Sandwich boxes content and many internal links will be deleted for media clients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Datelines: when to use place names and formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Use place names in datelines when reporter is near the scene, when significant reporting from multiple sources justifies it, for major market reports based in the market center, in-person interviews and analyses/features where byline/dateline add credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formatting: dateline indented four spaces, city in UPPER CASE, date and (Reuters) mixed case, a dash separates dateline from opening paragraph (e.g., NEW YORK, Sept 12 (Reuters) -). If in doubt about confusing readers, omit place name. Items without place names must still identify location in text and must carry a signoff tagline with reporter locations and editor (example provided). Do not use place names for stories largely written from press releases, webcasts, databases, pickups, or TV appearances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headlines: clarity, voice, tense and length
rubrics_metrics.description: Headlines must be sharp, clear and informative; for spot stories they should contain basic investor information; use active voice, present tense, short words and avoid unfamiliar abbreviations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Body of headline: sentence case (capitalise only first word unless a name). Headlines will turn red in Lynx Editor after 64 characters — use as warning. Prefer conveying one idea crisply rather than cramming two. Tags appear at start (see headline tags).

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline tags: single tag and tag formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Tags at the start of a headline give clients an idea of story type and should generally be in UPPER CASE followed directly by a dash then the headline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only a single tag (e.g., UPDATE 1- or ANALYSIS-). Exception: when correcting/refiling a tagged story, two tags can appear. EXCLUSIVE tag reserved for top exclusives and requires news editor approval. INSIGHT should reveal new information with original reporting; ANALYSIS must be based on reportage (not just author's ideas).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pool reporting: ground rules and byline conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: A pool is a limited group reporting on behalf of the press corps; ground rules and selection procedures should be defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three pool types described. If Reuters member wrote the pooled story use their byline and advisory line; if not, don't byline Reuters and file advisory line naming the pool and Reuters member. Add '(POOL)' to the slug for pooled stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedules/Skedlines: purpose and submission format
rubrics_metrics.description: Skedlines are offerings for schedules used by editors to compile the Schedule; the Schedule is a planning/presentation tool for media clients and editors, not a place to 'save' news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Skedline must state picture/TV availability, when story moved/is expected to move (time), and expected word count. Example format provided. World News and Business News schedule issue times and regional sked deadlines are specified. Desks may return to bureaus if the story is too long/late or requires images.
